title: Securing LLM-Agent Long-Term Memory Against Poisoning: Non-Malleable, Origin-Bound Authority with Machine-Checked Guarantees
title_zh: 保护 LLM-Agent 长期记忆免受投毒：具备机器验证保证的不可篡改、来源绑定权限机制
abstract_en: LLM agents increasingly rely on persistent long-term memory, which creates a critical vulnerability that we study here: memory poisoning. An adversary can store untrusted content in one session that later steers a consequential action, such as a payment, a setting change, or data exfiltration, in a future session. Existing defenses base a memory item's authority to act on either its content (detection or trust-scoring) or its derivation history (lineage). We show that both signals are malleable. An attacker can launder an untrusted origin through three channels specific to LLM agents: the agent's own summarization, a trusted-tool echo, and manufactured corroboration. Each makes the content look benign and breaks or flips its derivation edge to ``trusted.'' We formalize malleability for the memory write-retrieve-act pipeline and prove a machine-checked separation theorem. No content- or lineage-based defense is sound under laundering (T1), write-time origin binding is necessary (T2), and non-malleable origin-bound authority with Sybil-resistant corroboration-gated elevation is sufficient (T3). Our construction, TMA-NM (Tamper-evident Memory Authority, Non-Malleable), instantiates non-malleable information-flow control (IFC) for LLM-agent memory. A cross-defense, cross-attack, and cross-model benchmark over eight frontier models shows that existing defenses fail exactly where the theory predicts (up to 68% laundering attack-success), while TMA-NM reaches 0% attack success on both direct and laundering attacks across all models and channels, at full legitimate utility. We release the benchmark, harness, and machine-checked TLA+ models to support reproducibility.
abstract_zh: 本文研究 LLM agents 使用持久化长期记忆时面临的关键安全风险：memory poisoning。攻击者可在一次会话中写入不可信内容，并在未来会话中诱导 agent 执行支付、修改设置或数据外泄等高影响操作。作者指出，现有防御通常依据记忆内容本身（检测或信任评分）或其派生历史（lineage）来判断权限，但这两类信号都具有可篡改性。攻击者可通过三种 LLM-agent 特有通道“洗白”不可信来源：agent 自身摘要、可信工具回显、伪造佐证，使内容看似良性，并破坏或反转其派生边，使其被误判为“可信”。论文形式化了记忆写入—检索—执行流水线中的可篡改性，并给出机器验证的分离定理：在洗白攻击下，仅基于内容或 lineage 的防御不可靠；写入时来源绑定是必要条件；带有抗 Sybil 佐证门控提升机制的不可篡改来源绑定权限是充分条件。作者提出 TMA-NM（Tamper-evident Memory Authority, Non-Malleable），将不可篡改信息流控制（IFC）实例化到 LLM-agent 记忆系统中。基于 8 个 frontier models 的跨防御、跨攻击、跨模型基准显示，现有防御在理论预测位置失效，洗白攻击成功率最高达 68%；TMA-NM 在所有模型和通道上对直接攻击与洗白攻击均达到 0% 攻击成功率，同时保持完整合法效用。论文还发布了 benchmark、harness 与机器验证的 TLA+ models 以支持复现。
key_points_zh: 论文聚焦 LLM agents 的长期记忆投毒风险：攻击者可先写入不可信记忆，再在未来会话中触发敏感操作。
作者证明内容检测、信任评分和 lineage-based 防御都可被“洗白”攻击绕过，包括 agent 摘要、可信工具回显和伪造佐证三类通道。
提出并机器验证三项结论：内容或 lineage 防御不充分，写入时 origin binding 是必要条件，non-malleable origin-bound authority 加抗 Sybil 佐证门控提升是充分条件。
TMA-NM 将 non-malleable information-flow control 引入 LLM-agent memory，为记忆项提供不可篡改、来源绑定的权限控制。
在 8 个 frontier models 上，现有防御洗白攻击成功率最高 68%；TMA-NM 在直接与洗白攻击中均实现 0% attack success，并保持合法功能可用性。

llm_assessment.comment: This paper makes a major contribution to secure agent memory by formalizing poisoning risks and providing machine-checked defenses.
llm_assessment.comment_zh: 这篇论文通过形式化投毒风险并给出机器可验证防御，对安全的 agent 记忆系统有重大贡献。
